name: Pancharama Kshetras
theme: The five ancient temples of coastal Andhra where Shiva is worshipped as the shattered pieces of a single sacred linga
description: In the Shaiva telling, the demon king Tarakasura wore a Shiva linga that made him invincible, until Kartikeya, the young commander of the gods, learned it had to be shattered. The linga broke into five pieces that fell across the deltas of the Godavari and the Krishna, and where each came to rest a great temple rose over it — the five Pancharama Kshetras. At Amararama the immortals themselves gathered; at Draksharama the Sun kept vigil beside a towering crystal linga that is also a Shakti Peetha; at Somarama the Moon set a linga that still pales and darkens with the lunar month; at Ksheerarama a milk-white linga stands beneath one of the tallest gopurams in the land; and at Kumararama the boy-god's own linga climbs through two storeys of stone. Raised largely by the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi between the 9th and 11th centuries, the five are bound by one story and one mark — the scars the fire-weapon left on every linga. Four cluster within a day's journey across the Godavari districts; Amararama keeps its watch far to the southwest on the banks of the Krishna.
